title: Synchronization and Thread Safety
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of synchronization and thread safety in a C#/.NET program.
Predict the result of the included C# example and verify the documented output.
Apply synchronization and thread safety to a small task and identify one relevant boundary, limitation, or version requirement.

content.intro: Synchronization and Thread Safety is lesson 140 in Asynchronous Programming and Concurrency. Asynchronous methods let a caller await an operation without blocking a thread during I/O. Concurrency, parallel execution, and thread safety solve different problems.
content.why_it_matters: Asynchrony improves responsiveness; it does not automatically make CPU work faster or shared state safe. This lesson focuses on synchronization and thread safety and shows how to verify the behavior instead of relying on assumptions.

content.task: Try it yourself: create a small C# example that demonstrates synchronization and thread safety. Change one input or implementation detail, predict the result, then check it locally and explain one edge case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example demonstrates synchronization and thread safety rather than only repeating its definition.
The result is checked locally or against a clearly documented reference output.
At least one relevant boundary, invalid-input case, or compatibility condition is considered.
hints: List the assumptions and expected behavior for synchronization and thread safety before editing the code.

content.solution_notes: Suggested approach: identify the expected input and output, start from the smallest example, use the feature only where it clarifies the rule, and verify both a typical case and a boundary/failure case.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming the feature works identically on every target
common_mistakes.why: Language syntax, libraries, and runtime support are version-dependent.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the target framework and official versioned reference before using the feature.

common_mistakes.why: Boundary values, malformed input, and failure states often expose the real bug.
common_mistakes.fix: Add one typical input and one boundary or invalid case to the manual or automated checks.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating sample output as proof that the code ran
common_mistakes.why: The course reader uses static reference output for C# because it has no C# execution runner.
common_mistakes.fix: Run the snippet in a local .NET project or a separately isolated execution service.
